_README: What the field tells us that the GPS cannot. Keyed by survey unit —
'<Clan> — <Zone>', the same key the polygon layer uses. Everything here
is somebody's account, not a measurement, and it is reproduced as such:
on the clan's page under 'From the field', and in the clan's GPX so the
steward sees it on the device. Nothing here changes a geometry or a
figure. Add to it whenever the field answers a query.
Set 'river_boundary': true where a gap follows a large river. It stops
the pipeline asking the clan to walk it.
Named features are recorded only as the field spells them. Where a
name was read off handwriting it is confirmed before use, because a
misread river name propagates into every document and GPX after it.

notes: Large rivers cannot reasonably be walked. Boulders, rapids and steep drops make it physically difficult and unsafe, so a gap that follows one is not a gap anybody should be asked to close on foot.
Where a boundary is a large river, the survey team will complete that stretch themselves by editing. How to draw a robust river boundary is an open decision, not yet made.
The eastern border of Savasi's clan land is along the Baraje river.
The mapping is not finished: the northern and southern ends have yet to be closed off.
Four waterfalls lie along the boundary. From the north they are Ija, Taram, Pururi and Parari.
The river line itself is impassable because of those waterfalls, but the boundary follows the river line. That stretch is not to be walked; it will be completed by editing.
The smaller gap is a gorge at the Jarahe waterfall, and the two ends may be joined by a straight line. The straight line there is the boundary, not an assumption.

The river is resolved: it runs along the modelled drainage (2.48 km, kind river_routed). The Jarahe gorge is NOT resolved. A 1.86 km line adopted for it was withdrawn: it was not a break in the walk at all, but the span the closing step drew between two arbitrary points, running past all four open ends without joining any of them. The real open ends in Granville Nepo's walk are 44 m at the river, four ends 117-342 m apart where the western and north-eastern pieces fail to meet, and a 52 m stub.

Egobeyas Kuarisi and Granville Nepo walked this boundary together, both recording: 98% of each line runs within 50 m of the other. It is one walk recorded twice, not two walks to be joined. Joined, the linework doubles and the survey encloses 556 ha; taken as Granville Nepo recorded it, it encloses 1,099 ha and is closed but for 40 m.
Manuvoora — Zone 6.source: Field advice, 24 August 2026, on an annotated printout

notes: Closed without further survey. 217 m remained open and there is nothing there worth a return to the field, so the map is treated as finished. No track records that stretch, so it adds no walked distance. The clan has not seen this line and has not agreed to it — it is the survey team's judgement, not the clan's.
Four of Solomon Makanisa's tracks, 15.2 km, carry Lenard Urami's name in their attributes. Flagged, never reassigned — if the attribution is wrong the two stewards' distances are close to reversed.

This boundary was walked. What looked like 1.3 km of gap was the closing step drawing end-to-end across stretches the steward had already covered — every metre of it had walked line within 50 m. The eight loose ends are tied to the line beside them instead, 216 m in all, and the boundary closes on the walk.
PRIORITY: return to the clan. Both gaps, 788 m and 397 m on the eastern edge, need walking. Real gaps need real data; neither should be closed by editing.

Two real gaps, both on the eastern edge: 788 m and 397 m, where the recording stops and restarts with little or nothing walked between — only 37% and 31% of them have any walked line within 50 m. Both are easily fixed; a short walk closes them and no part of it is difficult ground.

A further 245 m of what is drawn is not a gap at all. Two of the four lines lie wholly within 50 m of ground the steward already walked, so there the boundary is recorded and only the ends need tying. That has not been done yet.

PRIORITY: return to the clan. The 917 m gap needs walking, not inferring, and the four interior lines need the clan to say which are boundary along the rivers and which are named places. Nothing here should be closed by editing.
One real gap, on the western edge by the Manoko boundary: 917 m, with only 12% of it having any walked line within 50 m. It needs walking.
Six other drawn lines, 966 m between them, are not gaps — they lie 82-100% within 50 m of ground already walked and only need their ends tying. Not yet done.

Four lines run inside the boundary rather than along it, and they are two different things. Two of them are the steward describing the boundary as following rivers — down the Salm to the Makamata fall, on to the Ujai, then up the Ujai to Sinigir. If that is the boundary, the mapped edge is in the wrong place along those stretches and the clan holds more than is shown. The other two are named places with histories attached. The clan needs to be shown the numbered map and asked which is which.
See output/queries/juaiko_to_clarify.png. The numbers on that map are deliberately not labelled; what each one is came from the stewards' own notes and is not for a document.
Walked by Unido Ose and Prut Buitari together; their two lines sit on top of each other for almost the whole boundary.

ASK THE CLAN: what is Jaginhul? Unido Ose puts the name on three recordings at the eastern turn on the north-east boundary, where both stewards leave the boundary line, make the same eastward excursion and both rejoin at the same place. The name is used for the whole stretch rather than for a single feature, and no water is named there. The nearest modelled watercourse is 818 m away, but that layer only resolves channels of about 0.01 km2 and up, so a creek crossed on foot would not appear in it. Knowing what Jaginhul is would settle whether the excursion is the boundary or a detour around something.
Chord 1 is a real gap: 203 m between Butam do and Muamara, where both stewards stopped and both resumed. Needs walking.
Riribudeh — Zone 8.source: Steward's own track descriptions, 15 July 2025; reviewed on the chord map 11 October 2026
Riribudeh — Zone 8.priority: Ask the clan what Jaginhul is; chord 1 needs walking

notes: Every stretch of this boundary that was walked is now followed rather than cut across. Three chords ran beside the steward's own line and are traced along it; three had no walked line between their ends at all — 144 m, 75 m and 26 m — and are straight joins, which is the whole of what can be said about them.
One real gap remains: 652 m on the northern shoulder, with no walked line between its ends. It is for the clan to close, not for editing.
No walked line falls outside the boundary.

NEEDS CLAN CONFIRMATION: a notch on the north-eastern edge, where a 2,120 m track crosses itself and closes a loop of 0.28 ha, about 109 m by 47 m, wholly inside the boundary. Nothing in the steward's notes says what it is. See output/queries/gumuyude_notch.png.
Walked by Max Mamo alone, 12 June 2025. His recordings name each stretch and the clan on the other side of it — Karira, Gubai, Suhikol, Anaje — which is the fullest annotation in the dataset.

Chord 5, 953 m, is a real gap: the Savahun boundary with Anaje clan, between two points Max Mamo named himself. It starts at the hook in the north where he wrote 'Sawahun broudre with anaje clan', at the corner where the Karira boundary ends. It ends at the Guaipnun waterfall, where three separate recordings stop and he wrote 'Savahun big drain so hard to continue over', 'Guaipnun hard to cross over.' and 'guapnun waterfall'. He could not get across. The stretch needs walking; it is not to be closed by drawing.
Dusi — Zone 8.source: Steward's own track descriptions, 12 June 2025; reviewed on the chord map 11 October 2026
Dusi — Zone 8.priority: Real gap — return to the clan

notes: GOES BACK TO THE CLAN TO REVIEW. Walked by Graham Ekiawa alone over nine days, 18.2 km recorded. Graham is from the clan, so the question goes to the clan with the map rather than to him on his own.
FOR THE CLAN TO CONFIRM: where does the boundary run across the north?

Four of Graham's five recordings are titled 'Mungaikol Clan land boundary' and form one continuous chain — 13 July down the west, 15 July along the south, 16 July up the east, 21 July on north — ending at the far north-east, 4.0 km from where it began. Nothing closes that 4.0 km.

His fifth recording, 20 July, 2.8 km, is titled 'Mungaikol Clan Sacred site boundary'. It starts 138 m from the chain's north-west end and runs east into the middle of the ground the chain encloses, stopping 3.2 km short of the north-east end.
So either:
(a) that line is the land boundary, and the unwalked stretch is the 3.2 km from its east end to the north-east terminus; or
(b) it is what he titled it, an unfinished sacred site perimeter, and the unwalked stretch is the 4.0 km across the north.

The two readings differ by roughly a third of the clan's land. There is nothing in the file to separate them: Graham wrote no comments at all, and no field of any recording mentions a river, creek, crossing or waterfall. Nineteen of the twenty-one sacred-site recordings in the dataset are open lines rather than closed loops, so the shape does not decide it either.
It has been suggested the boundary follows a river across the north. Graham can say whether that is so, and if it is, which river.
Until this is answered the pipeline closes the boundary using the sacred-site line as the northern edge and discards 5.4 km of the walked land boundary. That figure (338 ha) must not be issued.
Mungaikol — Zone 8.source: Raw recording titles and timings, 13-21 July 2025; reviewed on the chord map 11 October 2026
Mungaikol — Zone 8.priority: Back to the clan to review, 2026-10-14. No figure to be issued until they answer.

notes: LSS block — Land Settlement Scheme, the settlers. Treated as a
quasi-clan: it holds and is mapped like clan land, but it is not a clan
and must not be presented as one.
This matters for the overlap question. An LSS block lying over clan land
is not a fault in the data to be cleaned away — it is a finding, and
possibly the sharpest kind, because the ILG system assumes undisputed
single ownership and a settlement scheme on top of clan land is the
plainest case of that assumption failing. It must be measured, not
tidied.
Walked by Paul Digori, Zone 7A, 4.3 km in 13 recordings over May and
June 2026. His own words name roads, a house and a boundary marker:
'Dareki', 'Otherside.mainhighway.to.dareki', 'Myhouse', 'Block.home',
'Henry.and.justins.boader.cement'. The pipeline builds 282 ha from it
with 9 drawn lines, so almost all of that outline is inferred and none
of it confirmed.
It sits 0.00 km from Bimkol, Borori and Darekikol.

notes: SET ASIDE — too little data to work with.

Gibs Ginave recorded 1.4 km in five pieces, 1.07 km after smoothing. The whole of it spans 369 m east to west by 157 m north to south and encloses 1.45 ha. That is a fragment, not a clan boundary, and the two chords of 179 m and 106 m are closing a shape that was never a ring.
Two of the five recordings carry no name. The three that do say 'Darmal', 'Gibs Ginave / Land boundary' and 'Gibs_Ginave / Madukol Clan land boundary'. Nothing else is written anywhere in the files.
FOR THE CLAN: what was being recorded here? There is a tangle at the eastern end where the steward circled a small area several times, and no note saying what it is. And what is Darmal?
Nothing in this survey has been repaired. The 1.45 ha figure must not be issued as Madukol's land.
PRIORITY: two real gaps, 2.75 km between them, both on the western side. They need walking, not inferring, and nothing here should be closed by editing.

s2 — 1,860 m, the northern of the two. s10 — 890 m, the southern. Between them hangs a 727 m loop of walked line that touches nothing else, sits 658 m from the rest of the survey and encloses nothing. Peter Awako walked it; it is not joined to anything he walked before or after.

The question for the clan is the loop: is that ground Ambunkol's, and does the boundary run out to it and back, or does the line run straight past it? The answer decides what the two gaps actually are. Ask before anyone is sent to walk them.
Both stretches are in output/gpx/ambunkol_to_walk.gpx for the device. The rest of the boundary is settled: 16.51 km walked by Peter Awako, 0.17 km implied, 662.4 ha.
Reproduce the stewards' own wording in the report as it stands; the reviewer did not interpret it.

Jariji is also Zone 7B and not yet reviewed. The shared edge Nelson names is to be measured when Jariji comes round, not inferred now.

QUERY THE WHOLE SURVEY. These are not walked tracks. In the raw file Asoro's ten recordings carry 22.8 km on 177 points — an average of 129 m between them, and one leg of 7,418 m on ten points, 824 m apart. A walked GPS logs every few seconds. This is a set of points joined by straight lines.

The smoothed layer hides it: smoothing resampled every recording to a uniform 19 m spacing, so the map shows what looks like a track. It is not one, and the 21.54 km the pipeline reported as walked is not walked.
No polygon and no closing. Removed on 2026-10-15; the survey goes into the report as the recordings themselves, with this query attached.

Gilford Amakana recorded three surveys — Asoro, Majanko and Manoko, all Zone 2. The other two ARE real walked tracks, logging a point every 11-12 m. Only Asoro is made of joined points. That is worth putting to him directly: what are these points, and how were they taken?

s6, a 15 m recording at 652447 8989492, is not part of the clan land. That is the same place as the Afore Market knot in Ginangi's survey. s7 (2,726 m) and s9 (2,916 m) existed only to reach it and went with it.

It is attached at neither end — 240 m from the nearest point of the ring at its west end and 976 m at its east. The reviewer judged it not part of the polygon. It stays in the recordings and on the map, and the clan can say what it is.

s6, s8 and s11 were removed as wrong — 3,204 m of line that cut across the clan instead of following the southern loop the stewards walked. s7, a 30 m fragment, was left isolated by that and went too. s3 and s4 were also removed at the reviewer's direction.

Only one of the five recordings carries text: 146 m captioned 'Kennedy Wosa Bimkol Clan' and 'Dareki Village'. Dareki Village is the place named repeatedly in the neighbouring Darekikol survey. Nothing sacred or tambu.
